items.title: Albert Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: Dean Christian Gauss was a great mentor of literary people

ctx.x: Well I wish we could talk all day. But I know you have another engagement to go to. And so it’s really been fascinating, and an honor to have you here on campus. So on behalf of Hamilton College, I’d like to thank you and wish you the best in the future.

Well thank you. You know I feel like a grandson of Hamilton College because my favorite English teacher was from Hamilton. When I was a freshman, the guy that did a lot to inspire me to be a writer, or to embrace the field of literature and to become a writer, was from Hamilton. And I knew about Ezra Pound and people like that at Hamilton. And during that time Alexander Wolcott was a literary voice on radio and all, and he was Hamilton. And so I have always had a consciousness of Hamilton as a place of literary…
